title: Http2MultiplexHandler / Http2MultiplexCodec should not force the user…

timeline.message:
Http2MultiplexHandler / Http2MultiplexCodec should not force the user to provide an upgradeStreamHandler during client side cleartext upgrade

Motivation:

When we use Http2MultiplexHandler along with a clear tex upgrade in client side using Http2ClientUpgradeCodec, it throws an exception when a ChannelHandler is not provided for upgradeStreamHandler. This may be to strict as the user user can chose to create the outbound channel using Http2StreamChannelBootstrap later on.

Modifications:

- Just ensure we use a dummy handler that will release all received frames / events when the user does not supply one
- Adjust unit tests

Result:

Fixes https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/9508.
timeline.author: Norman Maurer

timeline.body:
… to provide an upgradeStreamHandler during client side cleartext upgrade

Motivation:

When we use Http2MultiplexHandler along with a clear tex upgrade in client side using Http2ClientUpgradeCodec, it throws an exception when a ChannelHandler is not provided for upgradeStreamHandler. This may be to strict as the user user can chose to create the outbound channel using Http2StreamChannelBootstrap later on.

Modifications:

- Just ensure we use a dummy handler that will release all received frames / events when the user does not supply one
- Adjust unit tests

Result:

Fixes https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/9508.
Why does this ignore/throw away the message, event, and exceptions instead of letting them go to the end of the pipeline?

reply.body: because the user has no way to access the Channel and so the pipeline to add handlers by himself / herself ?
Isn't that what the BootStrap will be in charge of, setting up the new stream channel?

timeline.body: @nizarm can you show us how you would make use of this ?

@nizarm, my understanding of your pattern is that after you get the signal to upgrade, you install `MultiplexHandler` and the frame codec and then immediately after use `Http2StreamChannelBootstrap` to actually spin up the child `Channel` as you would any other stream channel. This seems like a reasonable pattern to me, so I guess the open question is what to do for that upgrade stream initializer, eg the current pattern. Presumably we just don't want the `MultiplexHandler` to do anything if you haven't provided it, right? If so, the question then becomes what happens to the messages received the upgrade stream if you don't do bootstrap a new channel or bootstrap it too late (after messages have already started to flow through). Presumably we'd want to reset the stream in either case and log an error, or perhaps be even more aggressive since that situation represents a illegal state?

There is also a chance I'm misunderstanding so please feel free to put me back on course. 😄

Yuu got that right @bryce-anderson. Since the signal to upgrade happen only once and for every channel request by the user code we simply create a new streamchannel using the bootstrap shown above.
@bryce-anderson so I am right in my understanding that in this case we should just reset the upgrade stream directly ?

Good question. I asked because I don't think we should be adding the `NOOP_UPGRADE_HANDLER` which will silently discard messages. As far as I can tell, we don't want to initialize the stream channel at all since presumably the bootstrap will do that. At that point we'd need to change the `channelRead` methods to make sure we actually have an `.attachment` on the `FrameStream` before proceeding and if not reset and tear down?
@nizarm one thing that is not clear to me yet is why you can not just use the `upgradeHandler` as it is and want to use the bootstrap. Can you explain why this is ?

> @nizarm one thing that is not clear to me yet is why you can not just use the `upgradeHandler` as it is and want to use the bootstrap. Can you explain why this is ?

The reason is we maintain a channel pool that is responsible for returning Channels to downstream communication. If the connection is Http2 the 'upgradeHandler' based approach is not flexible for our use case - because that happens only once per non stream channel. But our channel pool would like to issue more stream channels on the parent channel using Bootstrap based approach !

> ```java
> bootstrap
> ```

Yes I can do this. But this will force me to have two code paths to create Http2StreamChannels. One during the upgrade time and the other one when every time the user want to write a new outbound message. The upgrade time happens only once during the lifetime of a parent TCP connection right?
@nizarm yes... It just feels cleaner this way imho... @bryce-anderson WDYT ?

I tend to agree with @normanmaurer. I think it's good to separate the upgrade stream from all other streams since it has some unique properties such as it's outbound data path being HTTP/1.x, etc. I'm not strongly opinionated about that, but it seems like the alternative is to risk some illegal state and guarding against that seems like it will spread the concern to a number of different places which isn't worth it IMO.
Ok let me close this one then...
